Maria G: quick heads-up: ran KV cache profiling on canary-nodes last night. warmup looks good for first 30s, then we see a fragmentation spike around 02:15 UTC and eviction churn climbs. attaching summary in thread (short notes below)

Aj Patel: saw that too from the metrics dashboard. frag_bytes jumped ~1.2GB in 5m window. eviction rate x4.

Kyle L: any recent kernel-path changes? could be batching change + different kernel causing larger temp allocations.

Maria G: yep, there was a small batching tweak (reduce-max-batch by 20%) and a kernel-selection tweak that prefers the fused-attn path for seq len<128. hypothesis: batched prefills + fused kernel alloc pattern causing slab fragmentation on GPU side.

Olivia H: logs (snip): `evict_count=12400 evict_ms=320 frag_bytes=1298748672 hotset_pct=83.4 prefill_rate=450rps`

Sam R: infra-bot reports deploy at 01:47 UTC: `deploy/eng-runtime v52 -> v53` with feature flag `adaptive-prefetch=true`.

Maria G: interesting — adaptive-prefetch flips on at deploy. Prefetch/decay heuristic probably increased prefill churn for some prefixes. I ran a small script to sample key lifetimes: `python tools/sample_kv_lifetimes.py --window 300` and saw median TTL ~12s but 10% of keys TTL <1s and that's causing hot churn.

Aj Patel: suggestion: try soft_ttl gradient instead of hard prefetch. config idea: `soft_ttl_ms=30000`, `prefetch_decay=0.55`, `max_prefetch_inflight=60`. small canary first.

Kyle L: also throttle prefetch when free_frag_bytes < 512MB to avoid amplification. pseudo-check: `if free_frag_bytes < 512<<20: prefetch_rate *= 0.3`

Olivia H: ran a quick sim with those params on local replay. result: eviction_count down 35%, average latency stable, but tail p99 token gen increased 8ms (within SLO). frag_bytes growth slowed.

Maria G: good. want to also test kernel-selection rollback: prefer older attention kernel when prefetch_rate>threshold to reduce peak scratch alloc. simple flag `kernel_sel=stable` vs `kernel_sel=aggressive`.

Sam R: can infra add a canary group with both configs: (A) adaptive-prefetch + kernel=aggressive + soft_ttl=default, (B) adaptive-prefetch + kernel=stable + soft_ttl=30s+decay=0.55 ?

infra-bot: created canary rollout `canary/kv-prefetch-2965437890` with 5% traffic, groups A/B split 50/50. monitors: kv_eviction_count, frag_bytes, p99_latency.

Maria G: experimental run plan: 1) 2h steady traffic test, 2) gather per-prefix hit-rate, lifetime distribution, frag growth curve 3) if frag_bytes delta < -200MB and evict_count down -> promote. otherwise revert.

Aj Patel: one more instrument request: add histogram for `alloc_size_by_kernel` so we can see which kernel path contributes most to large allocations. lightweight metric.

Kyle L: I'll add that metric and a quick alert rule: if frag_bytes growth rate > 50MB/5m then auto-scale-preemptive to shed prefetch (scale down prefetch threads).

Maria G: thanks. owners: Kyle adds metric+alert, Aj runs sim sweep for prefetch_decay values [0.4,0.55,0.7], Olivia runs the replay on canary data, I'll coordinate rollout and collect samples. follow-up in ~3h. :thumbsup:

Olivia H: noted. uploading replay results to drive: https://redwood-internal/replays/2965437890-prefetch-sweeps (brief csv + charts).

Sam R: tagging infra on-call (Kyle) in case canary alerts fire: @Kyle L

Maria G: final note — if we see repeated small-TTL keys causing churn, we should consider a short-lived bloom filter to avoid prefetch for keys with observed lifetime <2s. low-cost heuristic.

Aj Patel: agreed. low-risk guardrails first.

Kyle L: starting metric PR now.

Maria G: thanks all. I'll post a short postmortem-style summary after the run with numbers.
